name: Nayib Bukele
summary: Salvadoran president since 2019 who rose from the left-wing FMLN as a mayor, then governed as a self-declared neither-left-nor-right populist. He is defined by a mass-arrest campaign against gangs under a long state of exception, a supermajority that replaced the court and attorney general and ended presidential term limits, bitcoin adoption, sovereignty rhetoric against international bodies and NGOs, and socially conservative, openly religious positions.

sources.author: El Salvador in English

property-fundamental.rationale: Listed the right to property among the basic rights a society needs, and told the UN in 2024 that private property would always be protected in El Salvador; he did not discuss overriding it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Insisted that strict free speech means protecting speech one dislikes and criticised Western leaders who say some speech must be censored to protect the rest; he did not address hate-speech law as such.

strong-leader.rationale: Told CPAC the next US president needs the will and courage to do whatever it takes, and said change needs 'leadership' and a clear mandate; his own record is a supermajority used to replace the court and attorney general.

state-harmful.rationale: Treats the state as indispensable for security, infrastructure and economic development, saying internal security is the government's responsibility and promising state-led megaprojects.

limit-guns.rationale: Remarked approvingly that elites 'hate the Second Amendment' because a heavily armed population is hard to control; that is a comment on the US, not a Salvadoran gun policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: Doubled the army, re-equipped soldiers and police with vehicles and drones for the gang war, and told CPAC police should be encouraged to do their job without fear of repercussions.

rehabilitation.rationale: His flagship prison (CECOT) and tweeted measures such as removing mattresses and rationing food are punitive, and he put the rights of victims ahead of those of gang members; he proposed life sentences in 2026.

traditional-family.rationale: Said he opposes 'anti-God, anti-family' ideologies in schools and in 2024 dismissed culture ministry staff for policies incompatible with 'patriotic and family values'.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Answered 'no, not as a concept' when asked in 2020 and in 2021 withdrew constitutional wording that would have defined marriage as between 'spouses', keeping only the original one man and one woman.

abortion-legal.rationale: Said in 2020 he is not in favour of abortion and that it will one day be seen as a great genocide; in 2021 he declared the right to life from conception and ruled out any reform on it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Opened his 2024 plan with seeking God's wisdom, prays in cabinet meetings, and said God and morals should be reintroduced in schools.

gradual-change.rationale: Said economic fundamentals cannot change overnight without a mess, yet called for a total re-engineering of government and removed existing institutions' heads.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Told the UN in 2022 that its format is obsolete and that he no longer believes in it, insisting on absolute respect for sovereignty.

nation-first.rationale: Told CPAC globalism is dead in El Salvador and told the UN countries must make their own decisions, while saying his country wants open trade and friendly relations.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rejected rule by unelected bureaucrats and international experts, said international indicators such as GDP are 'fake', and credited the public's common sense.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His 2024 economic plan removed tariffs on certain agricultural imports for ten years to cut food costs; no broader statement on protecting domestic industry was found.

democracy-best.rationale: Calls himself democratically chosen, but replaced the constitutional court to run for a barred second term and has ruled under a state of exception since 2022; the record wins.

separate-church-state.rationale: Calls El Salvador a secular state, yet said both separation and union of church and state 'worked' in their time and pushes God into public life.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Repeatedly frames his policy as common sense judged by tangible results, says there is no single recipe, and that his own method fits his own reality.

national-rebirth.rationale: Describes El Salvador as 'reborn' after decades of violence and says the world needs to be reborn too.

universal-morality.rationale: Said there are fundamental values that are universal, grounded in God or in nature, such as that stealing and killing are wrong.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Said politicians' incentive to give away the treasury and run up debt (stimulus checks, relief) erodes both state and society, and pledged a 2025 budget with no debt for current spending.

national-self-determination.rationale: Quoted the UN Charter's principle of equal rights and self-determination of peoples and said each people should find its own way.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Names seeking God's wisdom as the first point of his plans and prays before decisions.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Argued that handing out money to people who do not work creates wrong incentives, citing US benefit and shoplifting policies; he framed work as the expected counterpart to support.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said the scale of corruption was what shocked him most in office and that most political systems, including rich countries', are corrupt; told CPAC corrupt judges and prosecutors served gangs.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Said it is important to reintroduce God into schools, which points away from excluding religion from state education.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Argued that unelected bureaucrats and NGOs have no democratic mandate ('who elected them?') and repeatedly grounds his authority in election results.

separated-powers.rationale: Told the UN that security policy required the executive, prosecutor and judiciary to be aligned on the same side, and his party removed the constitutional-chamber justices and attorney general in 2021.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Recalled in 2019 his father teaching that a country must work for the most vulnerable and that money is useless while people go hungry; no later policy statement was weighed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Defended the state of exception in force since March 2022 (suspending rights such as access to counsel and the 72-hour limit), crediting it for the fall in homicides; it has been extended dozens of times.

party-controls-media.rationale: Record: government pressure on independent outlets such as El Faro and expanded state media under his government; mixed toward agree.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Backs reuniting the Central American countries in a federal state and held the SICA presidency in 2019.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: His party passed constitutional changes in July 2025 allowing indefinite presidential re-election; in December 2025 he said he would stay ten more years if it were up to him, and in 2026 he sought a third term.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Has said Central America should be 'one single nation' and reaffirmed in 2024 that the five countries should unite, subject to the will of the peoples.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Argued institutions exist to serve the people, defended removing judges and the attorney general once voters gave him a supermajority, and said opposition-held bodies cannot block a popular mandate.

patriotic-education.rationale: Called for reintroducing morals and civics in schools and for patriotic values in public institutions.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said each country should design its own systems and no country may impose its way of doing things, while telling CPAC his model should not simply be copied.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: As a 2018 candidate he promised a pension reform to reverse the last reform that put the private fund managers (AFP) first; evidence is a campaign promise, and later reform details were not checked.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Proposed the foreign agents law in 2021 and the 2025 version taxing foreign funding at 30% and requiring registration, saying it limits foreign influence and protects sovereignty.

non-intervention.rationale: Told the UN no country has the right to impose its ideas on another and called for absolute respect for sovereignty, though he also offered troops to a UN-backed mission in Haiti.

religious-nation.rationale: Said in his 2024 inauguration that El Salvador is a secular country where non-believers may stay non-believers, although he professes belief.

religion-illusion.rationale: Professes belief in God, attributes national results to miracles and divine wisdom, and rejects the idea that religion is only an illusion.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Record: a foreign-agents law, pressure on independent media and NGOs, and journalists leaving the country under his government; mixed toward agree.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Ordered 'gender ideology' removed from public schools in 2024 and, in 2025, called allowing men to compete in women's sports a matter of common sense.

assisted-dying.rationale: In September 2021 he said his constitutional reform would not touch the right to life or allow euthanasia.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Declared in 2019 that the time of sides pulling in opposite directions was over and has said it is common sense rather than liberal or conservative; he told Time he is neither left nor right.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Credits God for his government's results and says he was on the side of 'God and the people', but also grounds his legitimacy in votes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Doubled the army and equipped it for domestic and Haitian deployments.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Wants God reintroduced in schools and says his cabinet are all believers.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Built the 40,000-inmate CECOT and said imprisoning gang members 'liberated millions'.

term-limits.rationale: Backed the 2025 abolition of presidential term limits and argued developed countries allow re-election; he is seeking a further term.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Framed the fight against gangs as a spiritual war he won and told CPAC that 'dark forces' were taking over the US.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Praised bitcoin and alternative systems as uncensorable and decentralised, protecting wealth from political decisions; he did not speak about government tracing.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Describes the gang war as both a physical and a spiritual war, said spiritual victory reflects in the physical one, and puts God's wisdom first in his economic plan.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Described the gangs as a parallel government that controlled territory, elections and parties, and built his security policy on dismantling them and regaining state control, including of the prisons.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Said his government changed the laws to make sure terrorists would not get out of jail again and backed a 2026 constitutional reform allowing life sentences for murderers, rapists and terrorists.

close-ties-china.rationale: Switched recognition to Beijing in 2018 and negotiated a trade deal with China, but is also a close ally of the Trump administration.

multipolar-world.rationale: Said a multipolar world would be better only if each people is free to build its own path, rather than moving from one superpower to several.

notes: As mayor he called himself part of the radical left; as president he disclaims any ideology. Positions on abortion and marriage hardened between 2014 (supportive of LGBT rights) and 2021. He told Time in 2024 he would not seek a third term, but the 2025 reform removed term limits and he registered for 2026. Several answers are low confidence because the record (foreign agents law, press pressure) conflicts with his stated positions.
